**Grant Application: Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant**

**Organization:** Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC)
**Request:** $15,000

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) respectfully requests $15,000 from the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant to expand vital gun safety education within Sacramento's communities of color. These communities disproportionately bear the brunt of gun violence and accidental firearm injuries, often lacking culturally relevant resources to address this critical issue effectively.

GAFC employs an innovative, multi-pronged approach to empower youth and families. Our "Gloxsie 21" animated series uses culturally relevant storytelling to demystify gun safety in an engaging way for children and teens. Complementary AI education workshops equip participants with essential digital literacy skills, fostering future readiness. Our hands-on community workshops, developed in partnership with the trusted Church of Legacy, provide practical, interactive firearm safety training directly where it's needed most.

Funding will enable GAFC to significantly expand our reach, aiming to educate over 500 residents within the Stockton Blvd corridor in the next year. Our projected outcomes include increased knowledge of safe gun storage and handling practices, a measurable reduction in accidental firearm incidents, and the cultivation of proactive community engagement in violence prevention.

As a minority-owned social enterprise, GAFC brings an authentic understanding of the specific challenges and cultural nuances required for effective intervention. Our unique blend of engaging media, technology education, and grassroots outreach, solidified by our deep partnership with the Church of Legacy, uniquely qualifies us to deliver impactful and sustainable change. We are committed to building a safer, more empowered Sacramento for all.
